content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx and streaming disconnect rate observed in us-west1 -> streaming-gateway. Paging SRE oncall. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream.

sre-oncall: acked — jumping in. Currently seeing alert from 12:33:40 -> 12:34:20 UTC.

maria.gonzalez: I can reproduce with `curl --http2` — chunked responses often end with `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` from client side. Server logs show a lot of 502 and 504. Sample nginx upstream log:```
2026-03-15T12:33:58.123Z us-west1 gw nginx: "GET /v1/stream HTTP/2.0" 502 0 "-" "grpc-web+json" upstream: "10.12.5.34:8080" upstream_response_time: 0.001, request_time: 8.256, "error: upstream prematurely closed connection"
```

ben: seeing similar. On the gateway, connection reset counts spike when backend latency > 3s. Also noticed increased RST packets in tcpdump on the gateway -> backend interface.

kate_p: customer-impact: two enterprise customers reporting partial transcripts and reconnects (CS ticket #3421, #3423). Support notifying customers now.

eng-runtime: quick hypothesis: when KV cache miss + large context, some model backends stall and the streaming proxy times out then tears connection. Could be request fanout causing head-of-line.

prod-ops: what's current mitigation plan? we should coordinate fallback and throttles.

ben: Suggested live mitigations we can do immediately:
- temporarily increase gateway streaming request timeout from 30s -> 60s (`gwctl set timeout --route /v1/stream --timeout 60s`)
- enable streaming->paged fallback for affected customer groups: `redwoodctl routing set-policy --gateway streaming --policy fallback-paged --selector region=us-west1`
- reduce concurrency per backend to avoid overload: `rtctl service update backend-stream --max-conns 80`

maria.gonzalez: I've enabled detailed debug sampling on 1% traffic for /v1/stream and captured a trace for req_id=req_352a. Trace shows backend hung while allocating KV cache allocation for token 1024.. more logs incoming.

eng-runtime: Can we force-route to an alternate model-variant (lower memory, faster) for canary traffic? If so we can confirm whether backend heavy kernels cause the disconnects. Command: `redwoodctl route override --target variant:llama-13b-8bit-fast --selector region=us-west1 --weight 5%`

support-lead: please add customer-facing note template. I'll push to CS. Priority customers asked for ETA.

sre-oncall: implementing mitigations in this order: 1) fallback-to-paged for region 1 2) increase timeout to 60s 3) throttle internal burst to 70% 4) enable debug sampling. Pushing commands now.

incident-bot: Deploy action: `gwctl` change applied by sre-oncall at 12:36:05 UTC. Rolling config to us-west1 gate nodes.

ben: after toggles we see 5xx rate drop from 4.5% -> 1.8% in last 90s, streaming disconnects decreased but not gone. Still seeing tail 504s on longer contexts.

maria.gonzalez: captured bumped logs show multiple `client aborted` entries with TCP FIN from client immediately after chunk N. That looks like client-side cancel but correlation shows gateway sent FIN first. tcpdump snippet:```
12:36:10.123 IP gw > backend: RST, seq 0, ack 0, win 0
12:36:10.124 IP backend > gw: RST, seq 0, ack 0
```

eng-runtime: That RST pattern suggests kernel-level ephemeral port exhaustion or aggressive conn-tracking on the gateway. Checking node-level metrics for conntrack and ephemeral range.

prod-ops: I'm scaling gateway pool by +3 nodes (bringing pool to 12). Also opening a temporary increased conntrack table size on gateways (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`) on the rolling nodes.

support-lead: Notified impacted customers with workaround: switch to paged endpoints or increase client socket timeout. CS will escalate if they request priority remediation.

sre-oncall: monitoring for 15m. If 5xx falls <1% and streaming disconnects <0.5% we'll start rollback of the fallback.

maria.gonzalez: collecting traces for 5 failure samples and uploading to #eng-runtime. Will paste request ids in thread when done.

ben: also enabling temporary gateway-level 502->503 fallback to dedicated/pinned routing for enterprise customers to reduce fanout. Command executed: `redwoodctl fallback enable --from gateway --to dedicated --tag enterprise --region us-west1`

incident-bot: Update: mitigation applied at 12:40:31 UTC. Post-mitigation metric snapshot: 5xx rate 1.6% -> 0.9% over next 60s.

prod-ops: continuing to monitor. Will keep scaling nodes until conntrack drain finishes.

eng-runtime: action items: 1) collect kernel conntrack metrics & tcp_retries2 over last 24h 2) analyze backend kernel logs for possible epoll regression 3) run isolated repro load against model variant to confirm stall.

support-lead: CS to follow up with impacted customers with timeline and temporary mitigations.

sre-oncall: leaving this thread open for 2 hours for observation. If anything regresses, page the SRE rotation and escalate to eng-runtime.

maria.gonzalez: uploaded traces: req_ids: [req_352a, req_352b, req_352c, req_352d, req_352e] to S3 bucket `incidents/3523456789/` and added links in #eng-runtime.

ben: thanks all. tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime @prod-ops.

support-lead: closing customer notification loop; CS will mark tickets with mitigation steps.

sre-oncall: marking as live-mitigation active. Will update once metrics stable or if rollback begins.
